still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived. Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Adults are ~275M, so 16.4% is ~45.1M current users, down from ~53.3M. Ever-used stays at 28.8% (~79.2M vs ~78.3M in 2032). About 2.9M first-time starts over two years, minus ~2.0M deaths among ever-users, leave a net gain of ~0.9M, which only keeps pace with population growth. Off now: 28.8 − 16.4 = 12.4 points (~34.1M). About 3.6M of them are on a planned 'holiday' they say they will end. Cycling: ~58% of current users are on a second or later course (9.5 points), and 3.0 points have cycled and are off again, so (9.5 + 3.0) / 28.8 ≈ 43% of ever-users have cycled. The other 9.4 points stopped once and have not restarted. This fits one-year persistence near one-third on weekly and daily products (~60% on clinic MariTide) and 36–47% restarting within a year, offset by planned holidays that have not ended yet. Age check: 0.20×8.5 + 0.33×15.5 + 0.24×24 + 0.23×16.5 = 1.7 + 5.1 + 5.8 + 3.8 ≈ 16.4. Income thirds average ~16.5. FICTIONAL payer mix (45.1M): commercial ~11.0M (5.0M of them in monitored tracks), Medicare ~11.4M, Medicaid ~3.0M, legitimate cash (TrumpRx, direct, telehealth) ~13.7M (including ~1.9M on quiet-mind or AUD-coded telehealth plans), imported or counterfeit ~6.0M. Sum = 45.1M. The bottom third fell 14 → 11 because gray-market users who stopped after bad batches or price spikes did not restart and lost-coverage workers did not replace them. The top third fell 25 → 22, mostly through holidays and long-term semaglutide users stopping after the litigation ads. Adult obesity is ~34.6%, up as regain outpaces new starts. About 24% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug. Pediatric: ~1.3% of under-18s are on a drug (12–17 ~2.7%; 6–11 ~0.4%, of whom ~0.22 points are on liraglutide and ~0.18 on Wegovy since its March 2034 6–11 approval). About 5.2M children under 18 live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

The dementia route is ~2.0M × ~$235 × 12 ≈ $5.6B. Oral amycretin has no Medicare-coverable indication. Medicaid: the same 7 states cover weight-loss use. ~3.0M users are mostly on diabetes codes, and two state programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Wegovy for 6–11 is covered under Medicaid EPSDT with growth-chart prior authorisation.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide (vials and, from 2033, tablets) sells for $4–30 a month. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $18–55. Canadian and Brazilian generics run CAD 45–80 and BRL 160–280. No generic amycretin exists anywhere. India and China supply about two-thirds of world incretin volume.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity is realised through an existing approved molecule in a new form. Novo filed oral amycretin in Sep 2032 on phase 3 data (~20.5% weight loss at 72 weeks, statistically non-inferior to tirzepatide 15 mg in a head-to-head arm), and the FDA approved it in Oct 2033, 13 months after filing. It is a daily pill with a fasting requirement and the first oral at injectable-class efficacy. The mood_and_motivation driver is realised through the approval of the oral semaglutide AUD sNDA (filed Jan 2032, approved Feb 2033). It is the first on-label reward-modulation indication, and Novo's 'quieter evenings' campaign plus telehealth quiet-mind plans market it as such. No standalone mood indication exists. Lilly began a phase 3 of orforglipron in binge-eating disorder in 2034 that will not read out before 2036. The pediatric_under_12 driver is realised by Wegovy's 6–11 sNDA (filed Sep 2032 on STEP Young data, approved Mar 2034 with growth-monitoring labelling). Bimagrumab-type muscle adjunct (filed Jul 2032): the 2034 advisory committee split 7–6 and a decision is due 2035. Tirzepatide dementia confirmatory topline is 2035. Implants are still phase 1–2. The global incretin market is ~$178B (2033). US net prices fall 3–5% a year, and brands hold ~$150–300 cash.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. Oral amycretin's nausea rate during titration (~40%) is comparable to injectables.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. It is pleaded in most mass-tort complaints anyway.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; consolidated into the expanded MDL.

safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language on semaglutide, tirzepatide and amycretin labels.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). Tirzepatide's excess is still non-significant at 6 years. Amycretin has no long-horizon data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide EPI warning (Mar 2031) retained; tirzepatide still under review. It is the core of failure-to-warn claims for pre-2031 use.

safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; Wegovy 6–11 approval carries a new 10-year growth registry requirement.

safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts maintained; CBP seizures flat near 2031 levels; no statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The liraglutide 24-month deficit of ~0.7 cm/year persists at 36 months, with partial catch-up in children who stopped. In STEP Young (semaglutide 6–11), height velocity was ~0.5 cm/year below placebo over 68 weeks. The Swedish ARFID signal (HR ~1.8) held in an update. Final adult height is still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Wegovy 6–11 approved (Mar 2034) for severe obesity only, with 6-monthly growth velocity, Tanner staging, eating-disorder screening and a required discontinuation review if velocity falls below the 10th percentile. The AAP kept its lifestyle-first interim guidance for prepubertal children. EMA review continues.

food_and_beverage.state: About 32% of US households now have a current user, down from 36%. Snack and confectionery volumes recovered slightly to ~7–9% below 2025, and sugary drinks to ~8% below. Kroger and Albertsons zip-code planning persists, but 'GLP-1 friendly' bays are being renamed 'protein' as regainers in lower-income stores push value-pack volume up. Mondelez cited 'holiday rebound' baskets in two quarterly calls.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are ~13–14% below 2025 and beer ~9% below. The 2033 AUD approval lets employer EAPs and telehealth prescribe on-label, and heavy-drinker losses deepened. Constellation and Molson Coors wrote down mid-tier brands, and closures continue at small-city bars in the Midwest. Drinkers on holiday drink again, briefly, and distributors talk of 'holiday spikes'.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat. Portion-tiered menus are standard in casual dining. QSR value traffic is up in regain-heavy markets such as Memphis and Dayton. Some chains now offer 'holiday' promotions timed to January and July, when planned breaks cluster.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists stabilised as regain grew. Resale and stretch lines serve cyclers and holiday-takers. Mass retailers keep size runs by zip code but now stock two sizes deeper on each side.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing, and 'hold your lean through your holiday' coaching packages ($79–149 a month) are the new add-on. Premium DXA memberships run $250–400. Employer tracks still bundle InBody scans with clinic MariTide.

insurance.state: Employer weight-loss coverage is down to 24%, and coverage concentrates on diabetes, CV and OSA codes. Pharmacy trend is ~+4% as covered volume fell. Adherence vendors added 'clinician-sanctioned holiday' codes capped at 8 weeks a year at some employers. At others, holidays break the adherence record and cost the premium differential. Part D premiums rose modestly again.

pharma.state: US branded volume fell ~15% while revenue fell less because Amvela is priced at the top of the cash band and has a commercial mix. Novo regained share on oral amycretin and the AUD label but carries the largest litigation provision. Amgen's MariTide is flat with employer tracks. Lilly leads injectables and is waiting on dementia data. Indian makers expanded into semaglutide tablets for export.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on a drug is now the unmarked default among insured adults 40–65, and the body that needs explaining is the one that has changed back. A softening face at the office prompts the question 'holiday?', and 'yes, eight weeks' closes the conversation. 'Lost coverage' or 'my lawyer said stop' do not. Lean with muscle still means covered and coached. Regained after 50 means lost coverage, a bad batch or a long semaglutide history and a law-firm ad.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle remains the class uniform. In Charlotte's SouthPark and Ballantyne, women aged 45–60 treat the pill-and-coach routine as unremarkable as a dentist visit, and the status move has shifted to the well-managed holiday: off for July, scanned before and after, back on in August with lean mass held. In Memphis the cycler's body is common. Former gray-market users who stopped are regaining without a planned restart, and nobody there calls it a holiday. On the Columbus freight corridor, workers who lost employer coverage in 2034 moved to $179 TrumpRx pills or stopped.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter for users and longer during holidays. Hosts in upper-income suburbs ask 'on or off this month?' the way they once asked about allergies. Bread Alone claims ~700 congregations. School debates now centre on whether nurses should log growth checks for children on Wegovy.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: App profiles carry an on/off/holiday field. 'Lean-mass verified' badges remain a premium tier. Couples schedule holidays around anniversaries and trips, and therapists describe 'holiday sex' as a recognised, slightly mocked pattern.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Among insured users, appetite is a setting that can be lowered, raised or switched off for a month. Appetite that returns without a plan reads as failure or misfortune. Unmuted now argues mostly about holidays and the AUD-label marketing. MAHA legislators focus on the Wegovy 6–11 approval. Fat-acceptance revivalists stay apart and are gaining among regainers.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% of users on maintenance weight doses vs ~3% of controls, ~10% on retatrutide, now in the Adverse Reactions section of every incretin label. About 1 in 4 current users (~11M) report a dose step-down or planned holiday for mood, pleasure or libido, and ~3.6M are on a holiday at any time. About 1.9M people are on quiet-mind telehealth plans, ~0.7M of them now prescribed under the AUD label. The low-dose anhedonia rate remains statistically unresolved.
interior_life.framing: The flatness is a known side effect that people manage, discussed the way people discuss SSRI sexual side effects. People step the dose down or take a holiday. Telehealth sells the low end as a feature ('quiet mind'). Novo markets 'quieter evenings' on-label for AUD. Clinicians document 'reward-related adverse effect, dose adjusted'. Unmuted calls holidays 'parole'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 5.0M employees are in adherence-verified tracks. Where vendors recognise sanctioned holidays, managers approve them like leave. Where they don't, a holiday costs up to 30% of the premium differential, so line workers in Columbus-corridor warehouses stay on and senior staff take breaks. The EEOC ADA charges remain without determination. One was withdrawn after a confidential settlement.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir has become a holiday genre, built on the month when everything came back: food, drink, grief, desire. A Netflix limited series, 'Eight Weeks', follows a Charlotte family whose members take holidays at different times. Unmuted off nights have spread into ordinary bars as 'holiday nights'. Sportsbooks see wagering surges from accounts in insured suburbs in January and July.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: The most common couples-therapy complaint has moved from mismatch to unsynchronised holidays. One partner comes off and wants more, and the other is still on and doesn't. Some couples now schedule holidays together. Sex-therapy practices advertise 'holiday planning'.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: MAHA-aligned legislators held hearings on the Wegovy 6–11 approval and the anhedonia labelling and passed nothing. No state legislature acted on adherence premiums or holidays. The mass tort supplies the most visible political content: plaintiffs' ads run in every media market. Turnout evidence for a 'sedated electorate' remains absent.

state.regulatory_posture: Routine and permissive. FDA approved oral semaglutide for AUD (Feb 2033), oral amycretin (Oct 2033) and Wegovy for ages 6–11 (Mar 2034). It added anhedonia to Adverse Reactions (Jan 2034) and kept telehealth focus claims under untitled letters. No state acted, Illinois's ban remains the only one, and Congress created no coverage, mandate or premium rule.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx operates on manufacturer-set prices. The Medicare Bridge pilot was not revived. The 2027 tri-agency 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law. Wellness vendors now ingest holiday codes alongside fills and clinic administration records. Telehealth quiet-mind platforms collect mood check-ins and use AUD diagnosis codes, which places part of that data under 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality and complicates its sale to benefit brokers. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules unchanged; Army recruit oral pilot continues without expansion. DOT has still not ruled on AUD-labelled or quiet-mind use among commercial drivers, although the AUD approval made the question on-label.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply about two-thirds of world incretin volume. Indian semaglutide tablets now enter US mail alongside vials. US–India talks still list CBP mail enforcement without agreement. Amycretin has no generic source anywhere, which keeps Novo's oral premium intact.

FDA approves oral semaglutide to reduce heavy drinking in alcohol use disorder; within weeks Novo's 'quieter evenings' campaign and telehealth quiet-mind plans begin prescribing under the new label

FDA approves oral amycretin as Amvela, the first pill to match injectables on weight loss; it lists at $1,199 but launches at $299 a month through TrumpRx, and ~3.2M users take it by end-2034, most of them switchers

After an FDA observational study finds dose-related anhedonia at maintenance doses, every incretin label adds 'anhedonia/reduced interest' to adverse reactions; surveys find one user in four has stepped down a dose or taken a holiday

FDA approves Wegovy for children 6–11 with severe obesity, requiring six-monthly growth checks and a discontinuation review if height velocity falls below the 10th percentile; the AAP keeps lifestyle-first guidance

open_tensions: Wegovy is now approved for six-to-eleven-year-olds while the liraglutide growth deficit persists at 36 months and final adult height is unknown. Monitoring is most rigorous in families most able to decline the drug.

Holidays are the accepted remedy for the flatness, but adherence-premium contracts in many firms penalise them, so blue-collar enrollees stay on and salaried staff take breaks. No one knows what repeated holidays do to bone, pancreas or regain.

The mass tort has split: gastroparesis claims lost a bellwether and EPI failure-to-warn claims won one. Settlement pressure on Novo is rising, and long-term semaglutide users are stopping or switching on lawyers' advice rather than clinicians'.
The pill removed the needle and left the price in place. Amvela at $299 cash sits beside $4 Indian semaglutide tablets, and fake 'Amvela' is already in the mail.

prose.headline: On Holiday: America's New Pill Matches the Shot, and Eight Million People Have Put the Drugs Down Anyway
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 about one American adult in six takes an incretin drug, some forty-five million people. That is eight million fewer than two years ago, though the share who have ever tried one has not moved. Nobody stopped believing in the drugs. They stopped for ordinary reasons: their employer dropped the coverage, a lawyer advertised during the evening news, the flatness got to them, or they decided to take July off.

In October 2033 the drug that was supposed to change everything arrived. Novo Nordisk's oral amycretin, sold as Amvela, is a daily pill that took off about a fifth of body weight in its trials, as much as the best weekly shot. The needle stopped being a reason to refuse. Price still is. Amvela lists at $1,199 and sells for $299 a month through the government's cash channel, and most of its three million users are people who switched from an injection. The Wegovy pill's maintenance dose fell to $179, and the starting dose is still $149. Pills now make up well over half of all use.

Who pays changed further. Only a quarter of employers still cover the drugs for weight loss. What remains of commercial coverage sits on diabetes, heart and sleep-apnoea codes, or inside monitored plant-clinic programmes where the monthly shot is logged for the wellness vendor. Medicare still covers only the old codes, at roughly thirty billion dollars a year. The gray market shrank. It shrank because people tired of bad batches, and no enforcement campaign had much to do with it. Six million people still buy by mail, and the newest fakes are pills.

The flatness now has a name on the label. A federal study found that maintenance doses roughly double the rate of diagnosed anhedonia, and in January every label gained a line about reduced interest. The complaint was already common, and the label made it official. One user in four has turned their dose down or taken a holiday, usually four to twelve weeks off to feel things again: food, wine, sex, grief. Some employers' wellness vendors now code a sanctioned holiday like leave. Others count it as non-adherence and charge for it, so the warehouse worker stays on and the manager takes August off. Meanwhile the same reward-dampening effect has an approved use of its own. Oral semaglutide has been approved for heavy drinking since February 2033, and the telehealth quiet-mind plans now prescribe under that label.

In Charlotte's southern suburbs nobody remarks on being on. People remark on being off. The question at dinner is whether the host is on this month, and the acceptable answer when someone's face softens is 'holiday'. In Memphis the same face usually means someone stopped and no restart is planned. Grocery planners talk about holiday baskets. Bars and sportsbooks see surges in January and July.

The courts are busier than the legislatures. Nearly ninety thousand people have sued over gastroparesis, bowel obstruction and pancreatic damage. A Philadelphia jury found the gastroparesis science too thin. A New Jersey jury awarded eleven and a half million dollars to a woman whose pancreatic insufficiency developed before the warning reached the label. Novo has set aside about three billion dollars. No settlement exists.

In March the FDA approved Wegovy for children as young as six, for severe obesity only, with height checks every six months and a review if growth falls off. The earlier liraglutide children are still growing more slowly than expected three years in. Hearings were held and no bills passed. No state acted. From outside, the country looks settled into its routine: a pill each morning, a break each summer, and a lawyer's number on the screen.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Lena Hart takes her Wegovy pill at 5:40 with four ounces of water, standing at the sink, then waits the thirty minutes. It is the $179 one now. The plant-clinic MariTide ended in January, when Kessler Freight dropped weight management and kept the diabetes codes, and she doesn't have diabetes.

At the Grove City office Marcy from payroll is eating a full turkey club at 10 a.m. 'Holiday,' Marcy says, before anyone asks. 'Six weeks. Coach says I'll hold the lean.' Nobody says anything else about it.

At lunch Lena eats four crackers and half a cheese stick and feels nothing about it, the same nothing she has felt about most things since spring. Her husband Dale said so last week, not unkindly: you used to laugh at the dog.

On the drive home the radio runs the ad again. Diagnosed with gastroparesis or pancreatic insufficiency after taking a weight-loss drug? She has had the diarrhoea since 2031, back when she was on Ozempic. She writes the number on a receipt and puts it in the cup holder.

The pediatrician's portal has a message about Kayla, who is ten. The new approval, it says. Worth a conversation. Growth checks every six months. Lena reads it twice and closes it.

After dinner, which she mostly watches, she opens the TrumpRx app and looks at the Amvela price, $299, then at the pause button on her own refill. Dale is in the yard throwing the ball for the dog.

She taps pause. Eight weeks, it asks. She sets it to six, the same as Marcy.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Planned holidays of 8+ weeks recover ~40% of lost weight on average and restart is slower with each holiday.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: it sits badly beside the same entry's "half to two-thirds regain within 18 months", because 40% regained in about two months is far faster. It also makes the prestigious 'well-managed holiday' and Marcy's 'I'll hold the lean' hard to believe.

least_plausible_claims.quote: About 2.9M first-time starts over two years, minus ~2.0M deaths among ever-users, leave a net gain of ~0.9M, which only keeps pace with population growth.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: this is a convenient reconciliation that pins ever-used at exactly 28.8%. It needs a high death count among ever-users and very low new starts in a window with an oral launch and an AUD label.

least_plausible_claims.quote: ~0.18 on Wegovy since its March 2034 6–11 approval
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism: 0.18% of 6–11s is roughly 40–45k children within nine months on a severe-obesity-only label with growth-chart prior authorisation. Under-12 starts had been falling and AAP guidance favours lifestyle-first, so the speed is unexplained.

rationale.badness: Use falls to 16.4% through coverage loss and litigation, while regain rises (obesity 34.6%) and the 2032 inequalities persist in new forms.
